name: symfony/dom-crawler
input_api: new Crawler() then Crawler::addXmlContent(string) (DOMDocument::loadXML with LIBXML_NONET always added); the XML-mode Crawler is traversed with children(), each(), nodeName(), attr(), text() and filterXPath() with namespace discovery and registerNamespace()
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom DOMDocument::loadXML; shared with the standard libxml2 APIs and with sabre/xml
package_own_scope: Crawler XML-mode navigation and query mapping: the addXmlContent default-namespace rewrite check, children()/sibling() element traversal, attr()/text() whitespace normalizing, filterXPath() relativizing, findNamespacePrefixes() and discoverNamespace(). Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity decoding and namespace binding are libxml2.
family: libxml2 via PHP DOMDocument, shared with the standard path and sabre/xml

popularity.caveat: Cumulative package downloads are a package adoption proxy, not XML-specific uses; DomCrawler is mostly installed for HTML crawling and functional tests (symfony/browser-kit, Goutte-style scrapers), so most of these downloads are HTML uses. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path and sabre/xml.

caveats: Crawler's documented default-namespace prefix ('default') resolves to the last default namespace declaration in the document; the order control's <plain xmlns=""> leaves it unbound, so the harness registers default-namespace URIs as ns1, ns2, ... with registerNamespace() and keeps auto-discovery for prefixed names.
addXmlContent replaces every 'xmlns' with 'ns' when the text has no 'xmlns:' prefix declaration; both shared controls declare a prefix, so that rewrite is not exercised.
addXmlContent suppresses libxml errors and yields an empty Crawler for non-well-formed text; only valid controls were run.

AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay that runs the same Crawler harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4, with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c and PHP ext/dom/document.c and ext/libxml/libxml.c instrumented. The two controls differ in 357 stable tuples, all of which also differ when addXmlContent runs alone; Crawler navigation adds the same 59 tuples for both controls. The Xdebug package-line report covers Crawler.php only and is kept separate.

name: symfony/serializer
input_api: new XmlEncoder() then XmlEncoder::decode(string $data, 'xml') (DecoderInterface; Serializer::decode delegates to it). With the default context it calls DOMDocument::loadXML with LIBXML_NONET | LIBXML_NOBLANKS, rejects any libxml error or a DOCTYPE, skips comments and processing instructions, and returns the root element's content as a PHP array
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom DOMDocument::loadXML; shared with the standard DOMDocument path, sabre/xml (XMLReader) and symfony/dom-crawler
package_own_scope: XmlEncoder's DOM-to-array mapping: root selection and DOCTYPE rejection, '@'-keyed attributes with numeric type casting, '#' text next to attributes, grouping same-named siblings into lists, the item/@key convention, and the root's in-scope namespace declarations from a DOMXPath namespace::* query. Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity and CDATA decoding and namespace binding are libxml2.
family: libxml2 via PHP DOMDocument, shared with the standard path, sabre/xml and symfony/dom-crawler

popularity.caveat: Cumulative downloads of the whole Serializer component, rank 3 in the snapshot's 'xml' query. They are a package adoption proxy, not XML-decoding uses: most installs come with Symfony and API Platform applications for object normalization and JSON, and XmlEncoder is one of several encoders in the package. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path, sabre/xml and symfony/dom-crawler.

caveats: decode() returns the root element's content, not its name, so the summary has no root field; root descendants, attributes and text are compared.

Element and attribute names are qualified (prefix:local). Namespace URIs are reported only as the root's in-scope declarations ('@xmlns', '@xmlns:p'); declarations on descendants are not reported, so the order control's <plain xmlns=""> undeclaration is invisible and resolving plain through the root bindings would give the wrong namespace. The oracle therefore parses without namespace processing and keeps only the root declarations.

Same-named siblings are grouped into one list keyed by name, so document order is recoverable only when they are adjacent (true for both controls). Comments and processing instructions are skipped by default. Numeric attribute values are type-cast (version="1" decodes as int 1); the summary prints them with json_encode.
decode() uses LIBXML_NOBLANKS, rejects any libxml error or DOCTYPE with NotEncodableValueException, and was run only on the valid controls.

Xdebug covers 69 XmlEncoder.php lines on catalog-ns.xml and 70 on order-default-ns.xml; 5 differ (attributes plus text: 245, 247; top-level comment skip, empty element, PI skip: 136, 300, 311). AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay that runs the same XmlEncoder harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4 with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c and PHP ext/dom/document.c instrumented; XmlEncoder's own lines do not reach the AFL++ map.

name: veewee/xml
input_api: VeeWee\Xml\Encoding\xml_decode(string $xml, callable ...$configurators): array, documented as "Decodes an XML string into an array". It loads the text with Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString($xml, 0) inside disallow_issues (any libxml error or warning throws, wrapped as EncodingException) and converts the document element into veewee's PHP array format. The same loader backs Dom\Document::fromXmlString; Dom\Document::fromXmlFile and Reader::fromXmlFile/fromXmlString (XMLReader) are the documented file and streaming entry points
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString; shared with the standard DOMDocument path, sabre/xml (XMLReader), symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer
package_own_scope: Encoding\Internal\Decoder: the DOM-to-array mapping (qualified element names as keys, same-named siblings grouped into lists, '@attributes' with qualified names, '@namespaces' with each element's own xmlns declarations, '@value' for text next to attributes, leaf text via textContent) plus the Dom\Document string loader and libxml issue collection. Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity and CDATA decoding and namespace binding are libxml2; turning xmlns declarations into attributes is PHP ext/dom.
family: libxml2 via PHP Dom\XMLDocument, shared with the standard path, sabre/xml, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer

popularity.caveat: Cumulative downloads of the whole veewee/xml package (rank 13 in the snapshot's 'xml' query, 3 in 'xml reader', 4 in 'xml decoder'). They are a package adoption proxy, not xml_decode uses: the package also covers DOM manipulation, XMLReader streaming, XMLWriter, XSD and XSLT, and many installs come through dependents such as php-soap and saloonphp/xml-wrangler. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path, sabre/xml, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer.

caveats: xml_decode keys elements and attributes by qualified name (prefix:local) and lists each element's own xmlns declarations under '@namespaces' ('' for the default namespace), including the order control's nested <plain xmlns=""> undeclaration. It does not report namespace URIs per element, so the summary keeps qualified names plus indexed per-element declarations and the oracle parses without namespace processing; resolving the summary's names through its declarations reproduces expat's namespace-aware expanded names on both controls, so no namespace information is lost on them.

Information xml_decode drops by design: comments and processing instructions (the order control's top-level comment and <?audit?> PI), the CDATA/text distinction (note's CDATA comes back as plain 'x < y'), text of elements that also have child elements (whitespace-only in both controls; mixed-content text would be lost), and document order of non-adjacent same-named siblings, which are grouped into one list keyed by name (adjacent in both controls). All values are strings.

The harness calls xml_decode($bytes) with no configurators. Its loader runs Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString($xml, 0) inside disallow_issues, so any libxml error or warning raises EncodingException; it was run only on the two valid controls. The documented file and streaming APIs (Dom\Document::fromXmlFile, Reader::fromXmlFile/fromXmlString over XMLReader) were not exercised.

Xdebug covers 295 veewee/xml lines in 186 files on both controls, with identical line sets: 161 of them are single declaration lines of function files that src/bootstrap.php loads for every use, and 77 are in Encoding/ (14 in the Decoder\Builder\element.php builder). Both controls take the same decoder branches, so veewee/xml's own lines do not distinguish them.

AFL++ feedback is not package-own: the native overlay runs the same xml_decode harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4 with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c and PHP ext/dom/xml_document.c and document.c instrumented. The 361 tuples that differ between the controls all also differ under a bare Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString, and the 2 post-parse tuples are the same for both controls. ext/dom/namespace_compat.c was tried and left out: with it the maps held 1149/1273 tuples and one differing tuple appeared only when veewee's attribute traversal ran.

name: mtownsend/xml-to-array
input_api: XmlToArray::convert(string $xml, bool $outputRoot = false) (the README's documented entry point; the global xml_to_array() helper forwards to it), called with $outputRoot = true. It loads the string with DOMDocument::loadXML and default options, then walks the DOM from documentElement into a PHP array; '@root' holds the root tagName
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom DOMDocument::loadXML; shared with the standard DOMDocument path, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer
package_own_scope: XmlToArray's DOM-to-array mapping: tagName keys, grouping same-named siblings into lists and unwrapping single children, trimmed text and CDATA as strings, '@content' next to '@attributes' for text-only elements with attributes, attribute values keyed by DOMNamedNodeMap iteration key, and the optional '@root' entry. Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity and character-reference decoding, CDATA and namespace binding are libxml2.
family: libxml2 via PHP DOMDocument, shared with the standard path, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer

popularity.caveat: Cumulative downloads of the whole package, rank 30 in the snapshot's 'xml' query. The package's only function is XML-to-array conversion, but downloads count installs (often transitive, e.g. through the author's Laravel request/response XML packages), not XML-decoding uses. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard DOMDocument path, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer.

caveats: convert() returns no namespace information. Element keys and '@root' are DOM tagName values (prefix:local); attribute keys come from iterating DOMElement::attributes, whose keys are local names, so c:lang and p:currency appear as lang and currency; xmlns declarations are not attributes in the DOM and are absent. Neither control's four namespace URIs appears anywhere in the raw arrays (checked by the overlay build), the order control's <plain xmlns=""> undeclaration is invisible, and two attributes with the same local name in different namespaces would collapse into one key. The adapter reports these keys as returned; the oracle therefore parses without namespace processing and strips attribute prefixes rather than resolving namespaces.

Same-named siblings are grouped into one list keyed by name and single children are unwrapped, so document order is recoverable only when same-named siblings are adjacent (true for both controls). Comments, processing instructions and whitespace-only text are dropped. Values stay strings.

Each element keeps at most one text string: a later non-empty text or CDATA child overwrites an earlier one, and (by source reading, not run) text before a child element turns the element into a string, so assigning the child then fails with a PHP Error. Both controls have text-only or element-only content.
loadXML runs with default options and convert() checks no error: on malformed input libxml2 warnings are emitted and documentElement is null. Only the two valid controls were run.

Xdebug covers 40 XmlToArray.php lines on catalog-ns.xml and 39 on order-default-ns.xml (43 and 42 package lines with helpers.php); 1 differs (62, the '@content' wrap for a text-only element with attributes). AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay that runs the same convert harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4 with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c and PHP ext/dom/document.c instrumented: 1096/1218 tuples over 5 identical repeats, all 360 differing tuples also differ under a bare default-option loadXML, and the 2 post-parse tuples are the same for both controls. XmlToArray's own lines do not reach the AFL++ map; the parser family is shared with the standard DOMDocument path, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer.

name: saloonphp/xml-wrangler
input_api: XmlReader::fromString(string) then elements() (documented; returns Element DTOs keyed by element name); fromFile(path) and fromStream(resource) are cross-checked for the same summary
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/xmlreader (veewee/xml Reader) and ext/dom DOMDocument::loadXML (veewee/xml xml_decode); shared with the standard libxml2 APIs, sabre/xml and symfony/dom-crawler
package_own_scope: XmlReader matcher/query layer over veewee/xml and the Element DTO mapping: elements() matches the document element in a veewee Reader pull loop, takes its readOuterXml() string and decodes it with veewee xml_decode into nested arrays (raw qualified-name keys, same-name children grouped into lists, @attributes, @namespaces with non-empty URIs, leaf textContent), then converts those arrays into Element objects with namespaces folded into xmlns/xmlns:* attributes. Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity and CDATA decoding and namespace binding are libxml2.
oracle: projects/xml/php/saloon_xml_wrangler/oracle.py (Python expat without namespace processing: raw qualified names, non-declaration attributes in document order, declarations with a non-empty URI sorted per element, untrimmed text of elements without child elements)
family: libxml2 via PHP XMLReader and DOMDocument, shared with the standard path, sabre/xml and symfony/dom-crawler

popularity.caveat: Cumulative package downloads are a package adoption proxy, not XML parse counts; the package also ships an XmlWriter, and many installs come through Saloon HTTP integrations. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path, sabre/xml and symfony/dom-crawler.

caveats: Raw-name scope: element and attribute names are raw qualified names (prefix:local). The package exposes no namespace URI per element; declarations appear only as xmlns/xmlns:* attributes on the declaring element. The summary does not infer URIs.

veewee/xml's namespaces() builder drops declarations whose URI is empty, so <plain xmlns=""> in order-default-ns.xml carries no attribute and is indistinguishable from an element in the inherited default namespace. Recorded as package behavior, not repaired; the oracle scope excludes undeclarations.
The package does not keep the source order of namespace declarations; the summary sorts them per element by attribute name.
Same-name children are grouped into one list under their first occurrence, so non-adjacent same-name siblings would be reordered; in both controls the grouped order equals document order.
Text beside child elements (mixed content), comments, processing instructions and the XML declaration are not exposed. Leaf content is DOM textContent, untrimmed.

libxml2 parses each input twice: XMLReader reads the original bytes, then DOMDocument::loadXML parses the readOuterXml() serialization of the root element. Only valid controls were run; no malformed, vulnerability or resource inputs.

AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay that runs the same harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4, with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c, xmlreader.c and PHP ext/xmlreader/php_xmlreader.c and ext/dom/document.c instrumented. Both controls give stable maps over 5 repeats (1,889 and 2,053 tuples) and differ in 414 tuples; 368 already differ when the veewee/xml Reader pass runs alone over the original bytes, and elements() alone gives the same maps as the full harness. The family is shared, so these tuples are libxml2/PHP-extension feedback, not package-owned feedback. Xdebug covers 56 XML Wrangler lines (XmlReader.php 33) and 298 veewee/xml lines on catalog-ns.xml and is kept separate.
